CO2016B-P1-61.exp: Excel's IF takes exactly three comma-separated arguments in one set of parentheses: the logical test, the value if true, and the value if false. The other three options invent extra brackets or repeat the function, none of which Excel will parse.

CO2016B-P1-62.exp: The dollar signs in $A$1 lock both the column and the row, making it an absolute reference that stays pointing at A1 even if the formula is copied elsewhere. Absolute only fixes the address - the value still updates live, so option C is the trap.

CO2016B-P1-63.exp: Conditional Formatting applies the red font automatically to any value falling in the 0-100 band, and keeps doing so as the data change. Manually colouring cells is static and breaks the moment a value changes, and IF returns a value rather than a format.

CO2016B-P1-64.exp: Excel's Paste Special dialog offers Formulas, Values, Formats, Comments, Validation, column widths and more as separate paste options. Since all three listed items appear in that dialog, the inclusive answer is correct.

CO2016B-P1-65.exp: The Series dialog offers exactly four types: Linear, Growth, Date and AutoFill. Time is not one of them - it is only a Date unit distinction, which is what makes this option the plausible-looking wrong one.

CO2016B-P1-66.exp: A leading apostrophe forces Excel to store the entry as text, so 007 or a phone number keeps its exact form; the apostrophe itself is not displayed or printed. The other symbols have no such effect.

CO2016B-P1-67.exp: Area, Line and Pie are all standard Excel chart types, alongside Column, Bar, Scatter, Doughnut and others. All three being valid makes the inclusive option correct.

CO2016B-P1-68.exp: Pointing at a cell on another sheet is referencing, written as SheetName!Cell - for example =Sheet2!A1. Updating and accessing are not Excel terms for this, so referencing is the defined vocabulary word being tested.

CO2016B-P1-69.exp: A slide-title master pair is the slide master together with its matching title master belonging to one design template, so a presentation using several templates has several such pairs. They remain two distinct masters, not one merged slide, which rules out option B.

CO2016B-P1-70.exp: A trigger is an object on the slide that starts an animation or action when the presenter clicks it, letting effects run out of sequence. An action button that simply advances the slide is navigation, not an animation trigger.

CO2016B-P1-71.exp: Slide transitions are the effects that play as one slide gives way to the next - fade, wipe, dissolve and so on. Custom animation is the separate feature that animates elements WITHIN a slide, which is the standard confusion.

CO2016B-P1-72.exp: Editing the slide master applies the background image once and propagates it to every slide that follows the master. AutoCorrect has nothing to do with slide appearance, so All of these cannot hold; building a whole template is a heavier route to the same end.

CO2016B-P1-73.exp: The handout master controls the layout of printed audience handouts - how many slides per page, plus headers, footers, date and page numbers. Slide formatting belongs to the slide master, and the Word export layout is governed separately by the Send to Word options.

CO2016B-P1-74.exp: Ctrl+Home jumps to the very first slide, and Ctrl+End to the last. Page Up only steps back one slide at a time.

CO2016B-P1-75.exp: Holding Shift while dragging a CORNER sizing handle constrains the object so height and width change in proportion. Dragging a corner handle on its own does not preserve the ratio unless Lock aspect ratio happens to be ticked for that object, so the combined option (a) and (c) is not safely true - note that some published keys nonetheless mark it as the answer.
